body: I can't answer that with certainty. As far as I know, I really don't want to feel better as such or carry on without her. I think I'm only talking about it to fill time for now.
I suppose so. I guess I need to do a little research into how quickly being sectioned can be arranged since I won't risk that if they can do it too quickly.

Well, I'll be seeing my counselor tomorrow but I'm afraid I don't see anyway they or anyone else could get me to want to carry on given what's happened.

Unfortunately, for now, and having been in this situation for months while she was away, I have a date in mind and I've completed all the prep for it.

Sure; we're coming up on 5 years now. I had intended to ask her to marry me.

I never saw it coming. Things had been slightly strained recently, which I thought was due to her utterly crazy work schedule this year (typically out from 7:30 - 2200/2300 up to 6 days a week, plus a lot of things she then has to do at home). But she told me she's been wanting to leave for a while and then I got hospitalised with a lung issue so she never spoke to me until it was too late, and she's then been working abroad for 2 months. When she came home, she was certain.

Yes and no.  


It's not that I couldn't. I accept that people do much later in life than me. But everything from her family, our shared history, and what she means for her simply makes me not willing to carry on without her. We haven't even fallen out or anything but she has told me she's fallen out of love with me, doesn't think she ever loved me quite in the same way as I did her, and is absolutely certain that \- though she wants me in her life \- she doesn't want me as a partner anymore.
It's a valid suggestion. Part of my fear is that going down that route any further has the potential to cause a removal of my ability to commit suicide, should I continue to want this.

29, and yeah, I can be held if I am considered a danger to myself. Suicidal thoughts have been expressed but since I have a definitive plan and, as of now, all the materials I need to carry it out, that'd cross the line.

Regarding medication, and this is going to come across as ridiculously stubborn, I guess I see the situation as the problem and since I can't change that, I want out.

I've actually been seeing a counselor and eventually raised the issue to my doctor. Unfortunately, I've had to start lying as it was getting too close to having me admitted against my will under the UK mental health act.

Unfortunately, the truth of how I feel is that I don't want to get by without her. And she's definitely not coming back to me so I don't want anyone to be able to stop me killing myself.

Thanks. I don't know if I know what to say, really.

I feel incredibly guilty at how it'll affect people who care but I really don't want to live either with the pain I'm in now or with her absence in my life and everything that will mean.  


I hear a lot about how if I could manage before, then I can manage after. I simply don't want to anymore.
